title: U.S. Senate · South Dakota

context.text: This is the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Mike Rounds, who first took office in 2015. Rounds defeated Justin McNeal 75.8%-24.2% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. South Dakota's Democratic primary was canceled after Julian Beaudion ran unopposed for the nomination, but Beaudion subsequently withdrew or was disqualified before the general election; Brian Bengs, the 2022 Democratic Senate nominee, is running against Rounds in the general election as an independent.

summary.text: Mike Rounds is the Republican U.S. Senator from South Dakota, seeking a third term. A former insurance and real estate businessman, he served in the South Dakota Senate (1991-2000, including as majority leader) and as the state's governor (2003-2011) before his election to the Senate in 2014. He was re-elected in 2020 and won the 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born in Huron, South Dakota, in 1954, the eldest of 11 children; he has lived in the Pierre area since early childhood.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from South Dakota State University in 1977.
In the private sector he built an insurance and real estate business with offices across the state; Wikipedia identifies him as a former partner in Fischer Rounds & Associates.
Elected to the South Dakota Senate five times and served from 1991 to 2000, representing the Pierre area as minority whip (1993-1994) and majority leader (1995-2000).

Won the Republican nomination for governor in 2002 and was elected that November with 56.8% of the vote; he was re-elected in 2006 with 61.7%. He served as governor from 2003 to 2011 and chaired the Midwestern Governors Association in 2008.
Announced his Senate candidacy in November 2012 and won the 2014 Republican primary. He won the open seat in November 2014 with 50.4% of the vote and was sworn in on January 6, 2015.
Won re-election in 2020 with nearly 66% of the vote after defeating a Republican primary challenger, state Rep. Scyller Borglum, 75% to 25%.

According to his official biography, he serves on the Appropriations, Armed Services, Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Indian Affairs, and Select Intelligence committees. Wikipedia notes he co-chairs the Senate AI Caucus and was a member of the bipartisan Senate AI Working Group.

Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary with 75.8% of the vote over Justin McNeal, and received President Trump's endorsement in July 2025. He lives in Fort Pierre and has four children and 11 grandchildren, according to his official biography.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, chairs the Armed Services Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and the Banking Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment, and also serves on the Senate Committee on Appropriations, the Committee on Indian Affairs and the Select Committee on Intelligence.

summary.text: Brian Bengs is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and judge advocate officer, attorney and former Northern State University criminal justice professor. He was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2022, losing to John Thune, and is running in 2026 as an independent. He says he is campaigning on getting money out of politics and lowering the cost of living.

background.text: Is an enlisted U.S. Navy veteran and a retired U.S. Air Force officer (lieutenant colonel), and has lived and worked in the United States and abroad.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history and international studies from Iowa State University (1994), a J.D. from the University of Iowa (1996), a master's degree in history from Louisiana Tech University (2007), and a master's degree in international and comparative law from George Washington University (2007).
Served as an Air Force judge advocate general (JAG) officer, including as chief of general law/assistant general counsel for the Air Force.

Taught law and policy topics at the U.S. Air Force Academy, the International Institute of Humanitarian Law, the NATO School Oberammergau and Northern State University, where he was an assistant professor and criminal justice professor.
Later worked as a Wind Cave National Park ranger, according to his April 2025 campaign announcement.
Was the Democratic nominee for this U.S. Senate seat in 2022, losing to John Thune 69.6% to 26.1%.

Announced on April 30, 2025 that he would run as an independent in 2026; Ballotpedia lists the Democratic primary winner, Julian Beaudion, as withdrawn. Bengs describes himself as a husband and father and says he has been active in South Dakota civic activities.

priorities.text: Getting money out of politics, saying "Big Money" has corrupted the political system so regular people cannot afford the lifestyle their parents had.
Balancing the federal budget and paying down the national debt.
Making daily life more affordable, including establishing affordable and accessible healthcare and safeguarding Social Security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Lists establishing affordable and accessible healthcare among his priorities, alongside safeguarding Social Security and Medicare.
